_comment: The gate's corpus, as data and not as source, for a reason the gate found
about itself on its first full run.
Both lists below are lines that TRIP tools/instant.mjs's lint, by
construction: the probes are the positive control and each allowlist key
is the exact text of a finding being argued for. Held as string literals
in tools/instant-gate.mjs they made that file the worst offender in the
tree -- twelve findings, every one of them this file's own subject matter
-- and the only ways out were a self-exemption by filename or twelve
allowlist entries for the allowlist. A gate that has to exempt itself has
stopped being a measurement of the tree.
So: a corpus of defective lines belongs in data, where no detector reads
it as code. The same shape as tools/secret-scan.baseline.json next door,
`why` is the argument. A reader who disagrees with one deletes the entry
and the gate goes red until somebody repairs the line.

allowlist.why: Episode.id is a record identifier already written to this repository's trial artifacts; changing the day changes published ids
display: the dashboard day column, which means the day the owner would say the work happened
display: the parsed record day, rendered beside the local-time conversation it came from
display: the Resolved column of the published table

allowlist.text: meta.textContent = 'generated ' + R.task.generatedAt.slice(0, 10) + ' · ' + R.files.length + ' files · ' + R.generations.length + ' generations · ' + R.conversations.length + ' conversation' + (R.conversations.length === 1 ? '' : 's');

allowlist.why: display: the record view resolved caption
